newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE ends at record high, buoyed by Dow rally.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE ends at record high, buoyed by Dow rally.

text.p: London's FTSE 100 leading share index burst into record territory on Friday as signs that the Dow's bull run was back on track inspired UK shares to bound ahead.
The FTSE closed at an all time high of 4,275.8, up 47.4 points on the day and 57 points since the start of the week.

Dealers said the fate of the market next week depended on monetary meetings in both the UK and U.S. An interest rate hike on either side of the Atlantic could bring the FTSE tumbling back down to earth, they said.

"We've seen a great performance today which should restore confidence to a worried market," one trader said. "But it could still be a white-knuckle ride next week," the trader said. "There's still a chance rates could go up here or in the U.S., and the higher we are, the further we could fall."
The spectre of a sharp sell-off sparked by a U.S. rate rise will keep markets nervous ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday and Wednesday, dealers said.
February 4 is the three-year anniversary of an unexpected U.S interest rate hike which sent world stock markets reeling. Some analysts believe history could repeat itself.
Nerves will be further frayed by the UK's monthly monetary meeting on Wednesday, which could result in a UK rate rise.
